title: Equitable partitions of finite rectangular grids are symmetry orbits (Neuberger-Sieben-Swift Conjecture 5.6)
exact_endpoint: GridFinal6.mathdb_343536 : ∀ m n ≥ 1, (∀ r : Setoid (Fin m × Fin n), IsEquitable (G m n) r ↔ ∃ H : Subgroup (G m n ≃g G m n), r = orbitSetoid (G m n) H) ∧ (Nonempty (EqPart (G m n) ≃o Subgroup (G m n ≃g G m n)) ↔ HasFreeVertex (G m n)) ∧ (HasFreeVertex (G m n) ↔ ¬ (2 ≤ m ∧ m = n ∧ n ≤ 3)), with G m n the Mathlib box product of paths
scope: Neuberger, Sieben and Swift, arXiv:1908.05797 (SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. 19 (2020)), Conjecture 5.6, proved for all m, n >= 1: every equitable partition of P_m □ P_n is the orbit partition of a subgroup of the automorphism group; the equitable-partition lattice is isomorphic to the subgroup lattice exactly when a free vertex exists; and a free vertex exists unless 2 <= m = n <= 3.

substantive_reason: It resolves a published SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. conjecture, supported by the authors only by computation through m = n = 20. The new content is the first sentence for m, n >= 2 (equitable partitions of grids are exactly automorphism-subgroup orbit partitions), proved by a boundary-propagation argument: a saturated border neighbour-multiset rule, non-backtracking colour walks with corner timing, explicit dihedral witnesses and positive-layer propagation. The lattice statements and the exceptional squares follow. Significance is modest; the path case was already covered by Brito-Manoel (2026).
